newsitem.title: UK: CONOCO SAYS STARTS UK MACCULLOCH OILFIELD.
newsitem.headline: CONOCO SAYS STARTS UK MACCULLOCH OILFIELD.

text.p: U.S. oil major Conoco said on Monday it had started oil production from its delayed British MacCulloch project.
Conoco said it brought MacCulloch onstream on Sunday and expected to reach a peak flow of 60,000 barrels per day (bpd). The field originally was scheduled to start at the end of last year.
MacCulloch, some 250 km east of Aberdeen, is operated through a floating production and storage and offtake vessel, the North Sea Producer.
The vessel has 560,000 barrels of storage capacity.
Estimated recoverable reserves at MacCulloch are 58 million barrels of 32-37 degree API crude and 15 billion cubic feet of gas.
Processed crude is being transported by pipeline to the Elf-operated Piper B platform and then to the Flotta terminal in the Orkney Islands.
Associated gas is exported via Piper B and onward to the Frigg pipeline and the St Fergus terminal in eastern Scotland.
